open_points.subject: EffectApproval request coverage for multipart and headers
open_points.text: “the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again” contradicts “the `multipart/form-data` content type without its `boundary` parameter” and “the boundary is not part of it”; header names are also lower-cased and sorted in the description
open_points.question: Must approval cover the exact wire-level header and body bytes, or the normalized request description that ignores multipart boundaries, header casing and header order?
options: Cover the exact wire request, including boundary, header casing and order
Cover the normalized semantic description defined by A10 rule 7
Make wire serialization deterministic so the normalized description identifies exactly one wire request
open_points.default_guess: Make wire serialization deterministic so the normalized description identifies exactly one wire request.

open_points.subject: Raw file content digests
open_points.text: “Every content-derived identity and digest in this kernel is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the model's meaning facts” and “a caller holding bytes computes the facts first” do not define how arbitrary file bytes produce `value_digest` or `content_digest`
open_points.question: What exact bytes are hashed for a file fixture or spooled file, and which module owns that computation?
options: SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, computed by the module holding them
SHA-256 of a canonical JSON encoding of the file
The store computes and returns every file digest
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, with the store computing or independently verifying it.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file integrity contract
open_points.text: The operation promises “Complete and digest-checked before it is visible”, but its Inputs provide “the file's bytes and its port's media type” and no expected digest or size
open_points.question: Against what expected facts does `spool_file` check the published file, and is the returned digest merely computed or independently verified?
options: Compute digest and size while writing, then reread and verify them before publication
Require expected digest and size as additional inputs
Compute and return digest and size without a separate verification step
open_points.default_guess: Compute digest and size while writing, then verify the completed temporary file before publication.

open_points.subject: Output ordering of embedded model collections
open_points.text: “Every collection in an output is in store order unless the operation names another order”, while ports, nodes, edges and constants are embedded values with no individual store positions and A01 only says they are sorted before hashing
open_points.question: In what order must operations return embedded collections such as contract ports and flow nodes, edges and constants?
options: Canonical A01 order
The order of the first accepted submission
An explicitly defined order for each collection
open_points.default_guess: Return them in the canonical A01 sorting order.

open_points.subject: stop_required from run-continuation operations
open_points.text: “`stop_required`, returned up the call chain after the caller wrote its record” applies to unconfirmed sandbox cleanup, but the Errors sections of `runs.resume_run`, `runs.continue_after_approval` and `runs.continue_after_resolution` omit it even though each operation advances the run and may execute a function
open_points.question: Do these three operations propagate `stop_required` when advancement encounters unconfirmed sandbox cleanup, and what partial records remain observable?
options: Propagate `stop_required` exactly like `start_run`
Convert it locally to `internal_error` without exposing the internal result
Prevent these operations from executing newly ready function nodes
open_points.default_guess: Propagate `stop_required`; preserve the concluded NodeExecution and all earlier whole store changes, then have the surface answer `internal_error` and stop.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest failures
open_points.text: “a manifest record that cannot be read stops the start” but “a selected instance the record does not list fails nothing here”
open_points.question: Which malformed manifest states count as an unreadable record at startup—for example invalid JSON, a wrong or missing `service` field, missing capability data, or malformed instance data—and which instead count as an absent selected instance that is deferred until send time?
options: Fail startup on any malformed service record
Fail only on I/O or JSON parse errors and defer all structural faults
Apply the full A08 manifest-record checks at startup
open_points.default_guess: Fail on I/O, invalid JSON, or an invalid top-level service record; treat a valid record lacking the selected instance as deferred to send time.

open_points.subject: service_invoker base URL acceptance and joining
open_points.text: An instance address need only be “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”, while invocation uses “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path” and “Nothing else is normalized”
open_points.question: Are base URLs containing a path, query, fragment, user information or unusual authority spelling accepted, and if so what exact final URL and Host value result?
options: Permit them and concatenate the declared path literally
Restrict `api_base_url` to scheme, host and optional port with no query, fragment or user information
Resolve the operation path using standard URI-reference resolution
open_points.default_guess: Restrict the base URL to scheme, host and optional port, then append the declared absolute path deterministically.
